chunks: And Husayn ibn Abdillah informed me, from Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Safwan al-Bazufari, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ubays ibn Hashim, from Karam, from al-Fadl ibn Shaybah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I asked Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him)
"Is there a fixed time for this matter?" He said: "The time-fixers have lied, the time-fixers have lied, the time-fixers have lied."

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter, specifically referring to the reappearance (al-Ghaybah/al-Zuhur) of the Imam
key_terms.الْوَقَاتُونَ: Those who fix or determine a specific time

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about those who fix a time for the Imam's reappearance?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) emphatically rejects the notion of a fixed, immutable deadline for the reappearance, declaring 'the time-fixers are liars' three times to underscore the certainty of his statement. This highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the divine knowledge of the 'hour' and the human tendency to speculate on specific dates, affirming that the event remains within God's exclusive prerogate while awaiting the appointed moment.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 411 - Narrated to me Husain bin Ubaidullah from Abi Ja’far Muhammad bin Sufyan Bazufari from Ali bin Muhammad from Fadhl bin Shazan from Ahmad bin Muhammad and Ubais bin Hashim from Kiram from Fuzail that he said: I asked Imam Baqir (a.s):
“Is there a fixed time for reappearance?” He said: “The time-fixers have lied, they have lied, they have lied.”
